reason: Follow-up read-only fact-check of issue 13 after independent review attempt 7fa26510ab774ea78f3c42ef314886a6, scoped to: (1) the SPEC.md citation edit, (2) the single narrow production repair in challenge_admission()'s routing-asset resolution, and (3) substantiating the 25/95/35 execution-count claims via retained artifacts. FINDING 1 (citation fix, VERIFIED): commit 5d9f457 ('lock(13): correct independently reviewed callsite citations') removed the stale 'commands/nightshift-implement.md:244-246' and 'scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:169-170' line numbers from SPEC.md's normative paragraph, replacing them with unlined prose ('The canonical GREEN callsite in commands/nightshift-implement.md must pass --task \"$TASK\"...'); the underlying requirement text is otherwise byte-identical (diff confirmed, single hunk). This resolves both CONFLICT rows from my prior review without altering any requirement. Baseline-commit citations ('integration/nightshift at 44ad7cc4d6af7a30cde2b139d9ad25c19b41c2bf') remain at SPEC.md lines 4 and 182, unchanged. The cited semantic locations still hold in current code: commands/nightshift-implement.md:305 passes --task \"$TASK\" at the GREEN callsite, and scripts/nightshift-trajectory.py:134-135 (seal/gate) + 223-224 (--task engineer dispatch) match my prior review's corrected citations. FINDING 2 (routing repair, VERIFIED, narrowly scoped): scripts/nightshift-behavior-proof.py challenge_admission() (already committed at HEAD, no working-tree diff) resolves the routing path via Path(...).resolve(strict=True) BEFORE read_json()/file_hash() (line 1203-1204), which follows a legitimate routing.json symlink to its real target instead of rejecting it outright. Post-launch validation is retained: challenge_proof() re-hashes the same resolved path after the reviewer subprocess completes and raises Blocked('challenge_provenance_changed') on mismatch (line 1310) - this is unchanged TOCTOU-style re-validation, not weakened by the repair (and per the task's explicit framing, this same-user filesystem check is not characterized here as a hostile-host security boundary). Proof/evidence/source symlink checks are separate functions (confined() at 154-170, private_file() at 222-232, plus the write_public()/regular() checks) and were not touched - confirmed by grep showing 20 call sites of confined()/private_file() spanning validation, scope, evidence, and receipt-write paths, none altered. routing.json's adversarial.cross_provider/routes structure referenced by the function exists as expected. FINDING 3 (execution counts): 25-case figure re-confirmed via static count (25 test_* methods in tests/test-behavior-proof.sh, unchanged). NEW: the 35-suite figure, previously NOT_FOUND for static corroboration, IS now staticaly verifiable without execution - evals/run-tests.sh discovers suites via `find tests evals/unit evals/integration -name 'test-*.sh'`, and running that same find non-executingly on the current tree yields exactly 35 files, matching validation-receipts.json's 'Summary: 35 passed, 0 failed, 35 total' and the format string at evals/run-tests.sh:27 exactly. The 95-assertion figure remains NOT_FOUND for static corroboration: tests/test-agent-dispatch.sh's check() counter (line 76) is invoked from multiple for-loops (mutation cases, gear values, roles, copy/symlink install modes, malformed/error modes), so simple call-site grep (37-47 static check-sites) cannot reproduce a flat total of 95 without executing the loops - consistent with, not a reversal of, my prior finding. External retained log files referenced by validation-receipts.json and the two failed-operation stdout receipts (source_version_probe: development-run.stdout; symlink_routing_admission: challenge.stdout) were confirmed to EXIST via `test -f` (all six paths checked returned EXISTS), but their byte content could not be read in this session - every content-reading tool (Read, cat, head, tail, wc, python3 file I/O) against paths outside the /private/tmp/nightshift-hardening-managed/13 worktree was blocked by this session's sandbox/permission boundary regardless of dangerouslyDisableSandbox. This is an environment limitation of this follow-up session, not a finding about the artifacts themselves; I could not independently corroborate the 95/35/2.1.266 sha256-bound log contents beyond what is already recorded in the checked-in validation-receipts.json (itself a self-reported orchestrator artifact, author_id root-orchestrator/codex, not an execution I witnessed). Engine SHA256 3cdd53a30b5dab496a672d07aa9d3c9222bef81a2f00c5ac471842159ac00299 matches exactly the symlink run's oracle_sha256 in validation-receipts.json (line 327); copy/source runs bind a different oracle_sha256 (881e5058...), consistent with the task's 'source/copy acceptance binds the previous engine' framing. Symlink run shows 2 development + 2 final scenario observations (public-positive/public-negative development; private-positive/private-negative final) consistent with 'two development/two held-out cases'; a prior symlink_routing_admission failure (reviewer_admission_unknown, 0 launches/reservations) precedes the resumed run whose counters (development:3 final:2) are consistent with retained-not-reset accounting, though I could not read the raw stdout to confirm budget-counter arithmetic beyond the structured JSON fields. RECOMMENDATION: Same as before - the previously-approved production correctness holds; the two requested non-blocking citation corrections have been applied and verified; the routing-asset repair is narrowly scoped and does not weaken retained symlink/hash checks. Recommend APPROVE. The 95-assertion and full external-log-content corroboration remain open items for a session with broader filesystem read scope, not defects in the reviewed code.
